notes: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners for the year ending June 30, 1897. Curated: the granite-faced subway to the Museum, the Museum's opening and annexes, the new Park Lodge.

coverage.remaining: Not placed: the Big Tree Cabin moved back from the Japanese Garden entrance, the electrical works building beside the pumping works, Sweeney's Observatory on Strawberry Hill (no page), the Prayer Book Cross described (dated in an earlier report).

findings.address_as_written: subway beneath the Main North Drive
findings.description: Gray Brothers finished the subway beneath the Main North Drive, between Ninth and Tenth Avenues, that lets people on foot reach the Museum and Concert Valley without crossing the carriage and bicycle traffic: 132 feet long and 21 feet wide under a semicircular concrete arch, faced with granite from near Raymond carved with buffalo heads around the arches, to a design chosen by competition in January 1896.

findings.description: With a large annex to the Museum finished in November 1896 and gifts still pouring in, the Park Commissioners began a second annex, 70 by 30 feet, for a new picture gallery, and built a furnace and engine room to heat the whole building against damp and mildew.

findings.description: The new Park Lodge, on a rise on the north side of the main drive near Stanyan Street, was described as Moorish-Gothic: walls of coarse dark grey sandstone trimmed with lighter stone under red Spanish tile, entrance steps of red Sespe sandstone up to a tiled veranda, offices for the commissioners, superintendent, secretary and engineer on one side and the superintendent's family quarters on the other, with the commissioners' meeting room paneled in mahogany and leather and a half story above for the park band.
